# motionforge

> A deterministic, browser-native video scene engine. The canonical video is a serializable JSON scene document; rendering is a pure function of (scene, frame). Agents author and patch scene JSON; the engine validates, lays out, and renders it.

## Mental model

```txt
scene JSON + frame -> parseScene -> evaluateScene (keyframes) -> layoutScene (boxes) -> renderStill (Canvas2D) -> pixels
```

- Time is integer frames at `scene.fps`, never wall-clock seconds.
- A node is active for `[from, from + duration)` in its parent's local timeline; children's clocks restart when the parent appears.
- Keyframe `frame` values are local to the node and must be strictly increasing (validated). Numeric values interpolate; color strings (`#hex`, `rgb()`, `rgba()`) interpolate in RGBA space; transform lists (`translate`/`scale`/`rotate`) tween when function sequences and units match; other strings step. Easing: `linear`, `easeIn`, `easeOut`, `easeInOut`, `cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)` (x1/x2 in [0,1]), or `spring(bounce)` (bounce in [0,1); may overshoot mid-tween).
- Node `id`s are unique across the scene by contract — patch and diff scenes by id.

## Hard rules

- Never use wall-clock time or unseeded randomness in anything that feeds rendering.
- Emit `schemaVersion: 1` for new scenes. Legacy v0 input is accepted only through deterministic migration; never invent a future version.
- Only use style properties from the support matrix (docs/scene-format.md). Unknown properties fail validation — this is intentional; do not work around it.
- Prefer data keyframes over imperative per-frame code.
- After editing a scene, re-validate with `validateScene()` and read the errors; they state the path, the problem, and the fix.

## Minimal valid scene (JSON)

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "width": 1080,
  "height": 1920,
  "fps": 30,
  "duration": 90,
  "assets": {},
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "bg",
      "type": "div",
      "style": {
        "width": "100%",
        "height": "100%",
        "backgroundColor": "#101820"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "title",
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Hello motionforge",
      "style": {
        "position": "absolute",
        "left": 64,
        "right": 64,
        "top": 800,
        "fontSize": 72,
        "color": "#ffffff",
        "textAlign": "center"
      },
      "animations": [
        {
          "kind": "keyframes",
          "property": "opacity",
          "frames": [
            { "frame": 0, "value": 0 },
            { "frame": 12, "value": 1, "easing": "easeOut" }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Node types: `div`, `text` (requires `text` or metric-stable inline `runs`), `img` (requires `assetId` pointing at `scene.assets`; draws with `objectFit`/`objectPosition`), `video` (requires `assetId`; optional `videoStartTime` trim in seconds, `playbackRate` multiplier — `sourceTime = videoStartTime + (localFrame / fps) * playbackRate`, last frame holds past clip end — and `volume` 0..1 plus optional `volumeEnvelope` node-local gain points: a clip's own soundtrack is mixed into the export at `volume * envelope`, trimmed/retimed with the picture; rate changes pitch-shift), `audio` (requires `assetId`; optional `audioStartTime` trim in seconds, `volume` 0..1, `volumeEnvelope` node-local gain points, and `loop:true` to repeat source playback through the node window; no style/children/animations — placement is `from`/`duration`; mixed into the exported MP4's audio track, overlaps sum), `lottie` (requires `assetId` pointing at a self-contained vector Lottie document; optional `playbackRate`; expressions and external image layers are rejected), `effect` (requires a supported semantic `effect` name and bounded `params`; general effects are `cartoonBurst`, `confettiBurst`, `cloudPop`, `speedLines`, `neonAura`, `scribbleCircle`; audio-reactive effects require `params.audioAssetId`), `extension` (requires `extension: {name, version, params}`; use only identities advertised by the host registry; params must be JSON and match the advertised JSON Schema; never emit code or module URLs), `shape` (requires `shape` geometry: `rect`, `ellipse`, normalized `line`/`polyline`/`polygon`, or SVG `path` plus `viewBox`; paint with `fill`/`stroke*`). Any visual node may carry closed `clip` geometry or `{shape, inverted?, opacity?, feather?}` as a vector alpha `mask`. Lengths: number = px, `"50%"` = of parent, `"64px"`.

Asset workflow: loading is the only async phase. `const assets = await resolveAssets(scene, {extensions?})` (from `@motionforge/renderer-canvas2d`); for scenes with video, Lottie, or prepared extension nodes also `await prepareFrame(scene, frame, assets)` per frame (no-op otherwise; `exportVideo`/the player call it automatically); then `renderStill(ctx, scene, frame, { assets })`. Rendering media/extensions without resolved/staged resources throws; `exportVideo()` resolves assets itself when not given them. Font assets register under their asset id — reference them as `fontFamily: "<asset id>"`, one asset per family+weight, without `fontWeight`. Call `disposeAssets(assets)` to release decoder and extension resources.

Media resources: resolution loads reachable assets only. HTTP media is range-backed under explicit cache/image/decoder budgets. Assets may declare `sourceMode`, `proxy`, and metadata; preview prefers proxy while export defaults to original. Video `videoEndBehavior` is `hold` or `loop`; negative playback is muted visual-only. Audio/video nodes may set `audioBus`, `pan`, and `ducks`; scene `audioBuses` configure gain/pan/limiting. Use `audioCrossfade()` for paired fades. Waveforms are opt-in cached analysis, and default preview audio is chunked around the current play/seek position.

Animation playback: keyframe tracks may use `repeat` (0..1000 additional cycles or `"infinite"`) and `yoyo`. Scene `markers` map stable names to in-range frames. Use `timeline().sequence()`/`.stagger()`/`.marker()`, `motionPath()`, `seededSignal()`, `maskReveal()`, and the 38-entry `compileMotionPreset()` registry rather than hand-computing choreography. Always store the compiled keyframes; never put preset names, callbacks, or random functions in scene JSON. Use `{reducedMotion:true}` when the host/user requests reduced motion.

Styles implemented today: `width`, `height`, `aspectRatio`, `safeArea`, `minWidth`/`minHeight`/`maxWidth`/`maxHeight` (min wins over max), `position` (`relative`/`absolute`), `left`/`top`/`right`/`bottom`, `inset`, `padding`/`paddingTop`/`Right`/`Bottom`/`Left`, `margin` plus per-side overrides, `display: "flex"`, `flexDirection`, `gap`, `justifyContent` (`flex-start`/`center`/`flex-end`/`space-between`), `alignItems` (`flex-start`/`center`/`flex-end`/`stretch`), `backgroundColor`, `background` (solid or linear/radial/conic gradient), shape `fill`/`stroke`/`strokeWidth`/`strokeLineCap`/`strokeLineJoin`/`strokeDash`, `borderRadius` plus per-corner overrides, `overflow` (`hidden` clips children, follows corner radii), `opacity`, `blendMode`, `isolation`, `transform` (`translate`/`scale`/`rotate`), `transformOrigin`, `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `fontWeight`, `fontStyle`, `color`, `textAlign`, `direction`, `textShadow`, `textStroke` (`"<width> <color>"`, stroke before fill), `textBackgroundColor` plus `textBackgroundPadding`/`X`/`Y`/`Radius` (measured per-line pill backgrounds before stroke/fill), `maxLines`, `minFontSize`, `textFit` (`wrap`/`shrink`/`truncate`), `textOverflow` (`clip`/`ellipsis`), `lineHeight` (unitless = multiplier of fontSize), `letterSpacing`, `objectFit` (`fill`/`contain`/`cover`/`none`/`scale-down`, img/video/Lottie nodes), `objectPosition`, `imageRendering` (`auto`/`pixelated`), `pixelSize`, `border` (`"<width> solid <color>"`, inside the box, follows corner radii), `boxShadow` (one or more comma-separated `"<x> <y> [blur] <color>"` shadows; no inset/spread), `filter` (chain of `brightness`/`contrast`/`saturate`/`grayscale`/`sepia`/`invert`/`opacity` with number or `%`, `hue-rotate(<deg>)`, `blur(<px>)` — applies per node draw, not to the composited subtree), `zIndex` (integer; reorders sibling painting, never layout). Every validated style property is implemented.

Text is multi-line: explicit `\n` always breaks; words wrap to the node's box width using real font metrics; lines are spaced by `lineHeight` and the block is centered vertically in the box. Auto height is intrinsic: text without an explicit `height` is exactly as tall as its wrapped lines, so top-anchored text starts at `top` and bottom-anchored text sits above `bottom` (absolute nodes with both `top` and `bottom` keep the inset height; use absolute `fontSize`, not `%`, on auto-height text). Spaceless scripts (Chinese/Japanese) wrap by grapheme automatically; Arabic shapes and wraps correctly (use `textAlign: "right"`, avoid `letterSpacing` on cursive scripts); for cross-machine determinism register a `font` asset covering the script. For caption pills, prefer `textBackgroundColor` on the `text` node instead of wrapper divs with hand-sized widths.

## Example validation errors

```txt
nodes.1.id: Duplicate node id "title". Node ids must be unique across the scene so tools can patch and diff nodes reliably.
nodes.0.style: Unsupported style property. MotionForge Scene v1 supports a curated CSS-like subset; move unsupported behavior into supported transforms, layout, or extension nodes.
nodes.2.assetId: img nodes require an assetId that points at scene.assets.
```

## APIs

- `@motionforge/schema`: `parseScene(json)` / `validateScene(json)` normalize valid v0 or v1 input to canonical Scene v1; `migrateScene(json)` also returns source/target version and migration ids; `sceneSchema` is strict v1; `inspectScene()` reports features; `lintScene()` reports valid-but-suspicious warnings; `sceneJsonSchema()` is the canonical draft-07 schema shipped as `scene.schema.json`.
- `@motionforge/schema` patches: **edit scenes with `applyScenePatch(scene, patch)` instead of re-emitting whole documents.** A patch is an ordered op list addressed by node id: `{op:"setStyle",id,style}` (merge; null deletes a key), `{op:"setText",id,text}`, `{op:"retime",id,from?,duration?}`, `{op:"setAnimations",id,animations}` (whole-list replace), `{op:"insertNode",node,parentId?,beforeId?}` (node needs a unique id — namespace yours, e.g. `caption-7`), `{op:"removeNode",id}`, `{op:"moveNode",id,parentId?,beforeId?}`, `{op:"setAsset",asset}`, `{op:"removeAsset",id}` (rejected while nodes reference it), `{op:"setSceneMeta",width?,height?,fps?,duration?}`. Application is transactional and pure: any failing op rejects the whole patch with `{opIndex, message}` errors (misspelled ids get closest-id suggestions) and the input scene is untouched. Re-validate nothing yourself — the patched document is fully revalidated for you.
- `@motionforge/core`: `composition()`, `div()`, `text()`, `richText()`, `img()`, `video()`, `shape()`, `extension()` builders → `.toJSON()`; `evaluateScene(scene, frame)`, `layoutScene(resolved)`.
- `@motionforge/extensions`: trusted hosts use `defineExtension()`, `createExtensionRegistry()`, `preflightExtensions()`, and `extensionManifest()`; registry manifests expose exact versions, renderers, worker support, and parameter JSON Schema for agent capability discovery.
- `@motionforge/renderer-canvas2d`: `preflightCanvas2D(scene)` reports runtime requirements before loading; `resolveAssets(scene, {extensions?, worker?})` → `ResolvedAssets` (async, once per scene); `prepareFrame(scene, frame, assets)` (async, per frame, stages media/extension data); `renderStill(ctx2d, scene, frame, { assets })`; `disposeAssets(assets)`; `computeObjectFit()` and `videoSourceTime()` for geometry/timing math.
- `@motionforge/presets`: pure helpers compiling intent to scene data — `popIn`/`fadeUp`/`slideIn(direction)`/`pulse(options)` → keyframe arrays; `tiktokCaptions(words, { fps, highlightIndices })` and `karaokeCaptions(words, { fps })` turn ASR word timestamps (`{ word, startMs, endMs }[]`) into timed caption nodes. Prefer these over hand-writing animation JSON.
- `@motionforge/presets/macros`: `expandMacroNodes()` and `expandMacroNodeInput()` compile semantic macro nodes into ordinary scene data; `macroNames()` lists registered capabilities and `macroPromptGuide()` derives agent documentation from the runtime registry. Prefer macros for designed overlays, effects, B-roll, captions, subtitles, transitions, and countdowns.
- `@motionforge/authoring`: use `makeScene()`, `seconds()`, `publicAsset()`, and high-level nodes for programmer-facing scene modules. Use `textBox()` for prompt/CMS/user copy that may be long; it emits bounded text with safe-area placement, shrink fit, ellipsis, `maxLines`, and `minFontSize`. Use `parseSrt()` or `parseVtt()` plus `subtitleTrack(segments, { template })` for SRT/WebVTT/transcript cues. Use `captionTrack(words, { template })` for ASR word timings. These helpers still compile to ordinary validated scene nodes.
- `@motionforge/presets` choreography: **never hand-compute frame offsets across nodes — use `timeline()`.** `timeline().add(id, preset, { at? | after?: id, overlap?, gap? }).stagger(ids, preset, { every }).compile()` → `Record<nodeId, animations>`; entries default to starting when the previous ends; `compileToPatch()` emits ready-to-apply `setAnimations` ops for `applyScenePatch`. Offsets are applied as frame-0 holds, so entrance presets keep nodes hidden until their slot. All choreographed nodes must share the same `from`.
- `@motionforge/player`: `createPlayer({ context, scene, assets?, loop? })` → `Player` with `play()`/`pause()`/`seek(frame)`/`dispose()`, `currentFrame`, and `on("frame" | "play" | "pause" | "ended", cb)`. Wall-clock time exists only in its `FrameClock`; every painted frame is the same pure `renderStill` output as export.
- `@motionforge/export`: `detectExportCapability()`; `exportVideo({ scene, onProgress?, startFrame?, endFrame?, signal? })` → `{ blob, codec, audioCodec, totalFrames }` — in-browser MP4 via WebCodecs + mediabunny with the scene's audio nodes mixed into an audio track (gate on `detectExportCapability().videoEncoder`); `renderFrameSequence({ scene, context, onFrame })` — the underlying deterministic frame loop with µs timestamps; `mixAudioSegments()` and `collectAudioPlacements()` for audio math.
